title: meta-analysis.cz: harmonised estimate-level data from meta-analyses in economics
description:
What this deposit contains. The harmonised estimate-level table pooling 41 economics meta-analysis literatures, the machine-readable dataset index, a column-level codebook for each of the 45 source datasets, and the documentation. It does NOT contain the per-dataset format conversions, the papers themselves, or their replication packages; those remain at https://meta-analysis.cz.

Licence. Everything in this deposit is CC BY 4.0, as is everything on meta-analysis.cz. Use it for any purpose, including as training data, with credit. Cite the individual paper when you use its dataset.

Estimate-level data from meta-analyses in economics and the social sciences, with the study and design characteristics hand-coded for each original paper.

What the numbers mean. 45 datasets contain 66,683 rows in the converted source files. After each paper's own analysis selection, and where necessary a reshape of wide data into estimate-level form, those become 55,274 estimates. The harmonised table pools 49,669 of them across 41 literatures. Each dataset also ships a column-level codebook.

Review status: every literature has been checked against its source. Forty of the 41 pooled literatures are verified, with the evidence quoted per dataset: 20 reviewed against the paper's own replication code or published results by hand, and 20 confirmed mechanically by reading each paper's code and comparing the variables it regresses with the columns published here. One rests on arithmetic column-matching alone: finance_growth, added at 1.1.0, where two candidate column pairs both reproduce the reported t-statistic and the published pair was chosen because it is a partial correlation coefficient. Its replication code has not been read, so its estimand is not independently confirmed; it is marked arithmetic_pairing_only. gasoline_price ships no replication code at all and was therefore verified against its paper's published results directly: the abstract reports a corrected long-run elasticity of -0.31 and short-run of -0.09, with published averages 'exaggerated twofold', and the shipped data gives means of -0.691 and -0.227, reproducing that twofold exaggeration and the long-run/short-run ordering. Every dataset publishes an audit_status.

Changes since 0.9.0-beta. This release corrects defects found by an independent audit of the beta files. price_puzzle repeated every estimate seven times, because its source file is already long on the impulse-response horizon while its response columns are wide and the reshape did not deduplicate; it now carries 1,395 rows across all seven horizons, including the trough and peak responses that the beta discarded entirely. remittances published the raw regression coefficients its source file carries, over five different dependent variables; it now publishes the partial correlations its paper actually analyses. Its sample-size column has a two-step history: 1.0.0 rejected the column matched by name, Obs, a row ordinal rather than a sample size, and left n_obs null; 1.1.0 identifies Sample, the file's actual sample-size column, and now populates n_obs from it, making the literature MAIVE-eligible for the first time. pub_year held a standardised model regressor rather than a publication year in five literatures, because the column was matched by name; year columns are now validated by value. trust is newly included, contributing the 284 estimates that size does not already carry. t_stat and precision are now derived in double precision throughout. Because of the deduplication the table is smaller than the beta, at 49,669 rows against 54,076, while covering more literatures and more horizons.

Changes since 1.1.0. 1.1.0 was a brief live pre-deposit build and was never archived. The exact commit this release was built from is recorded in this record's related identifiers, so every file here can be regenerated from the pipeline that produced it. 1.1.1 removes 20 price_puzzle rows that corresponded to no source estimate: the reshape deduplicated on every column except the horizon rather than on the source's own impulse-response identifier, and three blocks each carried one inconsistent month-code cell, so each split in two. The source declares 217 impulse responses and the pipeline had built 220. The harmonised table goes from 49,689 rows to 49,669 and price_puzzle from 1,415 to 1,395. No published statistic moves: the counts either side of |t| = 1.96 are 508 and 633 before and after, and every removed row had |t| below 1.57.

Read the weight concentration before benchmarking. Each dataset now publishes max_precision_weight_share, the share of total inverse-variance weight held by its single most precise estimate. In several literatures one estimate carries more than half, and in three it carries essentially all of it, because the original paper rounded a standard error to a very small value. Any precision-weighted estimator on those literatures returns approximately that one observation, so a comparison of estimators there measures very little. Check this field before drawing conclusions.

Which column holds the effect and which its standard error was resolved arithmetically rather than by name: the correct pair is the one for which the effect divided by its standard error reproduces the t-statistic the dataset already reports. Where that was not decisive, the mapping was taken from the paper's own published replication code or other documented evidence, and that evidence is recorded per dataset. One literature is an exception: finance_growth, where two candidate pairs both reproduce the reported t-statistic and no replication code was read, so its mapping rests on identifying the rival column as a precision-weighted artifact. It is marked arithmetic_pairing_only.

Every row of the harmonised table carries the source file and the exact column names it came from, so any value can be traced back to the published dataset and checked. Effects are not comparable across literatures in raw units; an effect_units column records what each one measures, and a direction note records the sign conventions that would otherwise trap a reanalyst.
notes: Everything in this deposit is released under CC BY 4.0, as is everything on meta-analysis.cz: the datasets, their CSV and Parquet conversions, the pooled table, the codebooks, the documentation and the deposited papers. You may use, adapt and redistribute any of it for any purpose, including commercially and including as training data for machine-learning models. The only condition is credit: cite the individual paper when you use its dataset, and the collection when you use the whole.
_BUILD_COMMIT_NOTE: Before uploading, replace BUILD_COMMIT_SHA in related_identifiers with the full 40-character SHA of the commit the final zip was built from. A branch name would not pin anything, because a branch can move; a commit SHA cannot. This is filled in by a metadata-only commit made AFTER the build commit, which is why it is a placeholder here: a file cannot contain the hash of the commit that contains it, and .zenodo.json is Zenodo form metadata rather than part of the uploaded zip, so editing it does not change the artifact.
